_comment: Layer 2 findings this algorithm is KNOWN to have, pinned to their exact
shape rather than skipped -- and, below them, the four places the
tutorial does not determine the encoding.
A finding that is merely tolerated becomes invisible: the run goes green,
nobody reads the list, and a genuinely new violation arrives among the
old ones unnoticed. So the baseline is asserted in both directions -- a
new violating tensor fails, and so does one that has been FIXED, because
then this file is stale and should shrink.
As of the first build, both Layer 2 validators come back CLEAN for this
cascade: single assignment and UDF names. That is a positive claim, not

why: Clean. Unlike max-flow, no tensor is seeded at a literal generation
inside the cascade: S_0 is written by the INITIALIZATION block, and
Path_0 is not written at all -- an absent tensor is the empty path.
Every cascade Einsum writes either generation i or generation i+1, never
both, and no two write the same slice.

specUndetermined.where: E09 reads Col_c; E11 reads Row_r
what: CORRECTED. This entry first said six tensors were undeclared -- F, d*,
TPath, NewPathEntry, Col and Row -- and that was the wrong complaint.
Declaring an intermediate by its first appearance on a LHS is the house
convention, not an omission. Max-flow declares NINE tensors and uses
twenty-three: ActR, Adm, Delta, Lbl, NST, PushCand, InPush, OutPush,
HasAdm, Rel, NeiLbl, MinNeiLbl and NewD are all introduced exactly that
way. Set-cover declares sixteen, so by that measure it is the better
documented of the two. F, d*, TPath and NewPathEntry are all written
before they are read and raise no question the convention does not
already answer.
Col and Row are the different case, and max-flow has none like them:
they are READ and NEVER WRITTEN, by any Einsum or initialization. There
is no first-use-on-a-LHS to define them and no declaration either, so
nothing in the tutorial says where their values come from.
They also are not really data. Col_c is 'present at every c' -- the
universe of the rank C, which the rank's own extent already fixes. EDGE
appears to have no notation for an all-present indicator over a rank, so
the cascade reaches for a tensor and then cannot say what it holds.
encodedAs: bool/False tensors supplied by the host alongside A and InitS.
Not derived from A, which would be wrong: a column that no row covers
still exists, and dropping it would silently make an unsatisfiable
askTheAuthor: Should Col and Row be declared as inputs, or does EDGE want a way to
write 'every coordinate of this rank' without a tensor standing in?
mechanicallyCheckable: A tensor read by some Einsum, written by none, and declared nowhere has
no source. That is decidable from the IR alone and would have found
this without anyone reading the cascade -- a candidate Layer 2 check.

what: The registry's `lt` returns a boolean, but TPath feeds E06's partial
update to form Path_{i+1}, whose entries are DEPTHS.
The tutorial's own worked example settles which is meant: at i = 2 the
path is {R3:1, R2:2} with d* = 2, and Path_3 is {R3:1, R0:2}. The
surviving entry kept its depth of 1. It did not become True.
encodedAs: A user-defined `take_left_if_less` -- the left value where it is less
than the right, the output's empty value otherwise.
Deliberately NOT named `lt` and not aliased to it, so the operator
comparison against the surface form reports the divergence instead of

specUndetermined.status: WITHDRAWN -- this was never a finding. The tutorial is right.
what: Recorded as a divergence, on the claim that a union merge makes an
absent Path entry arrive at `ge` as None. It does not. The evaluator
passes `value_or_empty`, so an absent entry arrives as Path's empty
value of -1 -- and then the tutorial's union is not merely tolerable,
it is correct FOR the reason EDGE's empty-value rule exists:
Zero is present at every r, so every row enters the map;
an absent Path entry reads as -1; -1 >= 0 is False;
False is SelRow's empty value, so the row stays absent.
The rule does the filtering an intersect merge would otherwise have to
do, which is the point of having the rule.
WHERE THE None ACTUALLY CAME FROM: this repository's own
take_left_if_less, which returned None for a filtered point instead of
the output's empty value. That stored None as a VALUE in TPath, which
flowed through E06 into Path_{i+1} and only raised two Einsums later,
at E07. Both were changed in the same edit -- the UDF was fixed and E07
was switched to intersect -- and the fix was credited to the wrong one.
Changing two things and attributing the result to one of them is how a
correct specification acquires a false finding against it.
encodedAs: The union merge the tutorial writes. Re-verified: both worked examples
reproduce exactly, and 60/60 random instances agree with brute force.

what: `occupancy` is available to a StoppingCondition, not to an Einsum
expression, so this cannot be written as one Einsum.
encodedAs: An OR-reduction over the columns, then a negation against TrueConst.
Equivalent, and the equivalence is why the difference is allowed.
specUndetermined.askTheAuthor: Should properties be usable in expression position?

what: E16's `1(select-min-val)` is Knuth's S heuristic: branch on the most
constrained column. Replacing it with select-max-val changes NOTHING
about the result -- measured over 25 random instances, the full
solution SET was identical on all 25.
It is still a real difference from the specification. Measured over 36
larger instances: 142 iterations with min, 234 with max; min explored
fewer on 27 and more on 0.
So no answer oracle, however good, can defend this operator. Only the
comparison against the surface form can. This is the concrete case the
operator-comparison gate exists for.
